desks.title: Thesis chapter 2 — literature review synthesis
desks.description: Turning 14 sources into an argument for a street-tree cooling thesis: the source matrix, the themes, the gap the study fills, and a draft due to the supervisor.
desks.brief:
## Thesis chapter 2 — literature review

**Programme** Master of Environmental Science (research) · **Supervisor** Rosa
**Draft due** @+12d · **Length** 8,000–9,000 words, aiming for 8,500
**Research question** Does street-tree canopy lower peak summer surface temperatures equally across western-suburb streets?

### What this chapter has to do
- Show what is known about canopy cooling, and how it was measured
- Show who benefits — the equity literature is where the gap sits
- End on the gap this study fills: almost no street-level measurement in lower-canopy suburbs

### Where it stands
14 sources in the matrix, 10 read and noted. Cooling is crowded (5 sources); maintenance and cost has only 2. Structure agreed with Rosa @-6d. **Drafting starts @+2d, once the gap paragraph is sent: ten days to @+12d, about 850 words a day.** S11 arrives by interlibrary loan @+3d and slots into 2.3.

callout.title: Write the gap paragraph first
callout.body: Rosa's one request before the full draft: a single paragraph naming what nobody has measured. Draft 1 is in the note. Send it @+2d, then write 2.1–2.4 around it — not before.

rows.source: S01 Canopy and surface heat, satellite study
rows.takeaway: Cooling scales with canopy; weak below 15% cover

rows.source: S02 Street-level air temperatures, two summers
rows.takeaway: Air cools less than surfaces; leafy suburbs only

rows.source: S03 Shade and pedestrian comfort model
rows.takeaway: Comfort gains depend on street orientation
Species matters in dry years; leafy suburbs only

rows.source: S05 Review of urban cooling strategies
rows.takeaway: Trees beat cool roofs at street level

rows.source: S06 Canopy gaps by suburb income
rows.takeaway: Canopy tracks income across the metro area
Renters can't plant; they rely on street trees
Planting follows requests, which favours owners

rows.source: S09 Heat and health in western suburbs
S10 Lifecycle cost of street trees
rows.takeaway: Watering in the first 3 years is the main cost

rows.source: S11 Root damage and footpath claims
S12 Resident attitudes to new plantings
rows.takeaway: Support drops once leaf litter is mentioned
Shade on solar panels is a growing reason

children.label: Trees beat cool roofs at street level (S05)
No street-level data in low-canopy suburbs
Field data only from leafy suburbs (S02, S04)

blocks.p: Thirty minutes with Rosa on the chapter structure. Outline agreed; two things cut.

ul: Keep cooling short — it is well covered. Spend the words on equity, where the gap is
Resident views becomes one section, not two

ol: Read S09, S11 and S14; finish S08 properly
Draft the gap paragraph and send it to Rosa before writing anything else
Check APA 7th on citing a source quoted inside another source

blocks.quote: If the gap paragraph is clear, the rest of the chapter has somewhere to go.

notes.title: Gap paragraph — draft 1
notes.body: Most of what is known about street-tree cooling comes from leafy, higher-income suburbs, measured from satellites (S01, S06) or at a handful of street sites (S02, S04). Lower-canopy western suburbs — where residents are more likely to rent and less able to plant (S07) — are almost absent from street-level measurement. This study fills that gap with a summer of street-level readings across 18 streets in three western suburbs.

desks.brief:
## Semester exams — 18-day revision plan

**Course** Bachelor of Biomedical Science, year 2
**Exams** 4, from @+8d to @+18d · **Hours available** about 52 after two café shifts a week · **Planned** 50

### How the plan was built
Every topic got two numbers: its weight in the exam and my confidence out of 5. High weight (35% or more) plus low confidence (2 or under) gets the hours. Topics I'm already solid on get one review pass and a question set — nothing more.

### Order
1. Statistics first — earliest exam, two topics still shaky
2. Biochemistry — metabolic pathways is the biggest single risk
3. Physiology and Microbiology share the last week

### Where it stands
4 of 12 topics solid. Two timed Statistics past papers done: 58%, then 64%. **Regression is the weak spot** — it gets today's first block.

callout.title: Biggest risk: metabolic pathways
callout.body: 45% of the Biochemistry exam, and confidence is 2 out of 5. It gets 8 of the 50 planned hours and the mind map on this desk. First full pass by @+5d, then a timed past paper @+9d.

Timed past papers beat re-reading every time
Explaining a pathway out loud to Tariq showed exactly where the gaps were
Two units a day at most, never three

blocks.p: Two shifts a week stay, but none in the 24 hours before an exam. The shift before Biochemistry is swapped with Mia — she takes @+10d, I take her shift @+12d.
